chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Yahya, from Ali al-Qasir, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the origin of perfume, from what thing is it? So he said: 'What thing do the people say?' I said, 'They allege that Adam descended from Paradise and upon his head was a crown.' So he said: 'He was too preoccupied for a crown to be upon his head.' Then he said: 'Indeed, Hawwa combed herself in Paradise with perfume from the perfumes of Paradise before her error occurred. So when she descended to the earth, she loosened her hair, so Allah, the Exalted, sent upon what was in it a wind, so it carried it to the East and the West. Thus, the origin of perfume is from that.'

key_terms.عَقِيصَتَهَا: Her hair (specifically the plaited or gathered hair)

ai.seo_question: What is the origin of perfume according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects the popular folk belief that Adam descended with a crown, offering a poetic cosmological explanation for the origin of perfume through Hawwa’s combing in Paradise. This account highlights the Shia scholarly tradition of distinguishing between literalist interpretations and symbolic narratives regarding pre-lapsarian events, linking the physical scent of the earth to divine grace distributed across the cardinal directions.
